subject.title: fix(gateway): make scope errors machine-readable across clients

question: Should OpenClaw make the new `gateway-error-details` subpath and `@openclaw/gateway-client/browser` re-export the supported cross-client authorization-reader API while enforcing the newly centralized parameter-aware scope outcomes?
rationale: This is an additive but public protocol/client API plus a behaviorally significant authorization-policy consolidation; tests establish intent, but long-term API ownership and acceptable upgrade behavior require maintainer judgment.

options.title: Approve additive contract after direct proof
options.body: Confirm the exported reader as the supported client API and merge after a redacted restricted-scope transcript proves structured details and the legacy fallback.

options.title: Keep reader internal for now
options.body: Remove the public subpath/browser re-export and retain only internal consumer migration until maintainers choose a stable external client API.

options.title: Pause for narrower scope policy review
options.body: Split the parameter-aware authorization changes from the client-reader API if their upgrade semantics need separate owner review.

recommendation.title: Approve additive contract after direct proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the exported reader as the supported client API and merge after a redacted restricted-scope transcript proves structured details and the legacy fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The available merged and current history ties this person directly to the structured authorization contract and its follow-up consumer migration.
